name: Sonoma County

known.via: English Wikipedia "Sonoma County AVA" (redirects to "Sonoma County wine")

climate: Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

keyfacts: A county is a legal American appellation of origin in its own right, so Sonoma County can go on a label without being an AVA when at least 75 percent of the wine comes from there.
Sonoma County has 19 AVAs, reflecting its wide variety of climate and soil conditions.
In Russian River Valley, cooling Pacific fog usually arrives in the evening, often dropping the temperature 35 to 40 degrees from its daytime high.
Russian River Valley is known for cool climate varieties, notably Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
The Petaluma Gap pulls cool coastal air inland through a gap in the coastal mountains, and its wind and fog suit Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Syrah.

notes: Sonoma Cabernet tends toward anise and black olive notes.

blurb.text: Sonoma County's main grapes are Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Cabernet Sauvignon. It holds many AVAs, such as Russian River Valley, Alexander Valley and Dry Creek Valley.
